description:
Filed by worker-40cfc767 at the request of qa-8546c5ba, who raised it while approving task-1aa5a87b (the resources fence) and correctly ruled it OUT of that row's scope: widening the fence to `releasable` there would have killed that row's own effects/boundary DRAINING negative controls. This is the same defect class, one family over, and it is production-reachable on committed bytes at HEAD.

MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY AT bb6978b, on a file that is clean (`git status --porcelain apps/daemon/src/work/foundation-attempt-service.ts` returns nothing) — so this is HEAD behaviour, not anyone's WIP:

1. `recordTerminalEffect` has exactly ONE production call site outside its own module. `grep -rn "recordTerminalEffect(" apps/daemon/src --include=*.ts | grep -v "\.test\.ts"` returns two lines, and one is the declaration:
     effect-terminal-ledger.ts:204   (export function recordTerminalEffect)
     foundation-attempt-service.ts:163
   `:163` sits inside the PROVEN path, above `recordProvenFoundationAttempt` at `:197`.

2. The `unproven` function (`foundation-attempt-service.ts:211-221`) reaches `noteRelease` at `:217` via `settleFoundationAttempt`, with no `recordTerminalEffect` call anywhere on that path.

3. That path is REACHABLE, not merely representable — four production call sites: `:304` (prepare failed), `:326` (`launched === null`), `:339` (commit failed), `:344` (launch returned a non-ok result). The `launched === null` arm is an ordinary runner outcome, not an exotic one.

4. Consequence, and why it is not self-healing: `release-terminal-evidence.ts:242` derives `effectsTerminal = provenTerminal(effects)`, and `:251` computes `releasable: effectsTerminal && resourcesTerminal`. With no terminal effect ever recorded, `effectsTerminal` is FALSE forever, `releaseWork` answers DRAINING, and `commitRelease` pins the decision at `expectedVersion: 0` (`attempt-release-store.ts:213-218`, whose own comment reads "a second release on this aggregate cannot append"). `attempt-release-disposition.ts:222` states the rule directly: once `commitRelease` lands a decision there is no compensating path. So the row is UN-UPGRADEABLE — exactly the shape the resources case had before 1aa5a87b fixed it.

WHY THIS CLEARS THE FILING BAR (human ruling 2026-08-22, clause 2): a correctness defect reachable in production today, on committed bytes, with no compensating path once it lands. It is not merely representable and it is not defended by a live arm — that is what makes it a row rather than a comment. Priority mirrors the identical-class row it follows (1aa5a87b was CRITICAL); a permanent resource strand with no recovery is not a diagnosability nicety.

DELIBERATELY NOT PRE-JUDGED HERE: whether the fix is to record a terminal effect on the unproven path, to teach the disposition that an unproven settlement is conclusively terminal for effects, or to leave DRAINING correct and add an upgrade path. The first is NOT obviously right — the proven path's own comment at `:159-163` says the terminal is "derived by the runner from already-committed evidence", and an unproven attempt may have no such evidence, so recording one there could manufacture a durable fact the runner never asserted (the class of defect this epic already rejected once). The planning step must choose between these on measured grounds and say which, and why the other two are wrong.
definitionOfDone: The chosen disposition for the UNPROVEN path is implemented and the choice is JUSTIFIED IN THE DIFF against the two rejected alternatives, on measured grounds — not asserted. If the fix records a terminal effect, it must be shown that the recorded fact is one the runner actually asserted, never synthesized by the daemon (the manufactured-durable-fact defect this epic rejected once already).

A behaviour arm drives the REAL shipped service through each of the four unproven call sites (foundation-attempt-service.ts:304, :326, :339, :344) against a file-backed store, reads the release disposition BACK OUT OF THE STORE rather than trusting a return value, and asserts the attempt is not stranded: no path leaves a row whose only reachable disposition is DRAINING at expectedVersion 0 forever.
The PROVEN path's existing behaviour is unchanged, proven by a preserved positive control — a blanket 'everything is terminal now' change must not be able to satisfy both this row and the old arms.

The effects/boundary DRAINING NEGATIVE CONTROLS that task-1aa5a87b's approval depended on still pass unmodified. If any must change, the completion record quotes the arm, the old and new expectation, and why the old one was wrong — a green suite after silently re-pointing a negative control is not evidence.

MUTATION DRILLS, each applied ALONE with a byte-exact restore proven by an empty `git diff -- <file>` (SHA-256 before/after for any untracked file), each naming the test that must go RED: (a) revert the unproven path to its current no-terminal-effect behaviour — the new strand arm must red; (b) make the fix unconditional so a genuinely non-terminal attempt is also marked terminal — a negative control must red; (c) point the terminal record at a foreign attemptRef — the binding assertion must red. ANY GREEN DRILL IS A VACUOUS ASSERTION: strengthen it, re-run, and say so in the completion record rather than recording a pass.

`pnpm --filter @moe/daemon typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` is EXIT 0 on a fresh run, with the receipt quoted. If a foreign uncommitted red is present at gate time, attribute it by path with `git status --porcelain` and an `it(` title diff of HEAD vs worktree before reporting it — do not edit foreign WIP.
